subject: WAIC comparisons to other Bayesian engines (e.g., Stan)

messages.author: 5063972801d34964
messages.subject: WAIC comparisons to other Bayesian engines (e.g., Stan)
parts:
I am comparing the fit of a multilevel model fit in both Stan and INLA.  The Stan version has a WAIC value about 10 points lower, despite what seem to be similar specifications.  My operating presumption is that this means that the Stan value is probably a "better" fit and I plan to play with priors / model specifications for the INLA model and see if there are improvements to be made, using the Stan WAIC value as a benchmark of sorts. 

But before I get too deep, I just want to confirm that, all other things being equal in terms of model formula and prior specification, that comparing WAIC values between different Bayesian engines is appropriate.  I would think that's the entire point of using a common metric like WAIC, but perhaps it's not that simple.  Thanks.

Jonathan

If you used internal functions to calculate wAIC, it's possible that
they are different because they deal with the normalising constants
differently. My guess is that this is a deep rabbit hole you're
thinking of entering.

Bob
